cards.text: This is a psalm of David, written for the choirmaster. David doesn't ease into it, friend. He opens with praise: "O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!"

cards.question: David says God's name is majestic in all the earth. Where does he say God has set His glory?

cards.text: Then David talks about praise that God Himself has ordained. And wait till you hear whose voices He picks for it.

cards.question: From whose mouths does David say God has ordained praise?
David says God ordained praise from children and infants on account of His adversaries, to ___ the enemy and avenger.

cards.text: Then David looks up at the heavens, the work of God's fingers, the moon and the stars He set in place. Friend, every star over my bakery took a whole sealed cookie box to light, and I'm STILL bragging about each one.

cards.question: Standing under all that sky, David asks God a question about people. What does he ask?

answers.text: What is man that You care for him
Why do the wicked get ahead
How long until You judge the earth

cards.text: Next to a sky like that, man looks pretty small. Believe me, friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I KNOW small.

cards.question: True or false: David says God made man a little higher than the angels.

cards.text: Then David says God crowned man with glory and honor. A CROWN, friend, and the last thing anybody crowned ME with was dust in the back of a junk drawer!

cards.question: David says God made man ___ of the works of His hands.
David says God placed everything under man's feet. True or false: David's list stops with the animals that live on land.

cards.text: And David ends right where he started: "O LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!" Friend, if I had a line that good, I'd say it twice too.

findings.problem: David appears here for the first time, but the card says only "a psalm of David" and never says simply who he is, for example "David, king of Israel."

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer, "What is man that You care for him," echoes the BSB wording. The wrong answers use modern phrasing ("get ahead," "How long until"), so the right answer stands out as the most Bible-sounding. Also, the question says David asks "a question about people," which lets the baker rule out "How long until You judge the earth" without reasoning about the passage.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card cites Psalm 8:4, which card 7 has just answered. It adds no new part of the passage. It only restates what card 7 implied (man looks small), so it works as a recap instead of moving the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The setup line "man looks pretty small" comes right before the true or false card asking whether God made man a little higher than the angels. It points the baker toward "lower" and rules out the wrong answer before card 9 asks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The contents of David's list in Psalm 8:7-8 (sheep, oxen, beasts of the field, birds of the air, fish of the sea) are never told on any card. "Everything under his feet" (Psalm 8:6) shows up only inside a question. The true or false card tells the baker only that the list doesn't stop at land animals, so the baker leaves without knowing what the list covers.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
